summary: REQUEST_CHANGES on legitimate SWARM-PROTOCOL owner PR #329 exact head 275ba90dfe699e22b495b6f77086e8c6e845fd11. The patch removes the broad timestamp-only fallback for unlisted malformed events and correctly adds finite historical identities including SYNC_REQUIRED and MaterialDNA affects, but its strict-first ordering silently accepts the already-laundered normalized cart-review bytes instead of enforcing the audited first-write top-level slotId shape. In addition, semantic subset pinning is insufficient while failed immutable transitions can become future baselines; allowlisted historical exceptions need exact audited path/blob identity until trusted-history continuity is repaired.
evidence: Historical cart event at ref 54b28d6e6cd9de972cc63801a50b33a9ba0299dd has top-level slotId='audit'; current authoritative swarm-control has metadata.slotId='audit' and no top-level slotId after failed mutation ebc699fc416346e5a6dc6cc02f6d992b635f205f was later laundered into a PASS state.
PR #329 calls _STRICT_VALIDATE_EVENT first and consults _HISTORICAL_EVENT_COMPAT only on strict failure; the current normalized cart bytes therefore bypass the historical rule entirely.

Authority/WorldEntity/cart compatibility rules pin selected semantic fields rather than complete immutable blobs, leaving listed identities vulnerable to the already-confirmed failed-transition laundering class for otherwise-unpinned bytes.
